origins: After a setback, we often imagine what other people are saying. A family member’s silence, a former coworker’s awkward pause, or a friend’s “So what are you doing now?” can feel like judgment. If we grew up in a family where reputation mattered, the fear of being seen as a failure can be stronger than the loss itself.
teaches: Scripture warns that the fear of man is a snare, but whoever trusts in the Lord is set securely on high. Paul asks, “Am I now seeking the approval of men, or of God?” and says that we are approved by God, who examines our hearts. The psalmist says, “The LORD is with me; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?” This is not a call to ignore people. It is an invitation to anchor our worth in God’s view, which is steadier than anyone’s opinion.
self_statements: Everyone thinks I am a failure.
They are being polite, but they pity me.
I cannot face anyone I know.
They are better than me now.
errors: Assuming I know what others think.
Believing everyone is focused on my situation.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that people look down on me.
questions: What have people actually said to me, as opposed to what I imagine?
Who has treated me with kindness since this happened?
Would I think a friend was useless in my situation?
Whose approval matters most to me, and why?
What does God say about my worth?
What would help me face people with less shame?
truth: I cannot read other people’s minds, and most people are more focused on their own lives than on mine. God’s view of me has not changed. I can trust Him instead of fearing others’ opinions and let kind people help.
hw_truths: I do not know what others think.
The fear of man is a snare.
Most people are focused on their own lives.
I can face others with honesty.
log: Each week, write one thing you imagined people thought and what they actually said or did.
actions: List what people have actually said or done since the job loss.
Reach out to one kind person.
Contact someone who has been supportive and tell them what you are facing.
Write one honest sentence for “What are you doing now?”
Read it aloud before a hard conversation.
prayer: Lord, You see me as I am. When I fear what others think, steady me with Your approval. Help me answer honestly and receive kindness from the people You send. Amen.
hw_questions: Who has been kind to me?
What would I think of a friend in my place?
Whose approval do I most want?
What does God think of me?
What simple answer can I prepare?
name_example: Sarah can write: “The Lord is on my side, so I do not have to fear what others think.”
